Hi Samir  great to chat today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment for the pricing exercise: 

Summary of ask:
- You want us to price a Dedicated/Hosted mix for ACME’s production inference (chat + batch batch-rerank jobs).
- Key inputs we need from you to produce accurate unit economics: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, percent of requests requiring extended context (8k / 32k / 128k), and monthly token volume (prompt + completion).

Immediate questions (can you confirm these by EOD?):
1) Average prompt tokens (per request)  ballpark or sample distribution is fine.
2) Average completion tokens (per request) and typical max completion lengths.
3) Approx % of requests that must access >8k context, >32k context, and any that require 128k.
4) Expected monthly token volume (total tokens/month) or budget range (target $/1M tokens).

Notes on what we’ll produce after you send numbers:
- A side-by-side cost model (hosted vs dedicated) showing $/1M tokens, expected latency @ typical batching, and suggested quantization/serving profile.
- Recommendations for batching & caching to hit your target $/1M tokens.

Attachments: I can accept a CSV export or sample logs (anonymized)  either works. I’ve also included a short template (see sample_prompts) in the follow-up if you prefer to drop in a few examples.

Next steps:
- Samir: share the token profiling and any usage export (acme_usage_q2.csv would be ideal).
- We’ll return a draft unit-econ sheet and pricing target within 2 business days.

Thanks 

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing sketch assumptions for ACME (notes)

Marissa  copying a quick internal math sketch so we’re aligned before the client call. Keep this internal.

Assumptions from Samir: 180M tokens/month total; avg prompt 420; avg completion 260; mix: 84% 8k, 13% 32k, 3% 128k.

Ballpark unit-econ approach:
- Hosted baseline: assume $/1M tokens = base_hosted_unit (well run scenarios). With default batching & caching, expect ~2030% savings over naive per-token billing.
- Dedicated: fixed monthly commit buys lower per-token compute cost once utilization >60%. For 180M tokens, committed capacity likely makes sense if ACME wants predictable latency and cost.

Suggested client-facing targets to present:
- Conservative: $950 / 1M tokens (no dedicated commit, includes reserved 32k pool with cold-start buffers).
- Mid: $750 / 1M tokens (modest 612 month commit; 32k pooling; light quantization Q4).
- Aggressive: $600700 / 1M tokens (multi-quarter commit + dedicated pool with mixed precision quantization + KV caching).

We should show a sensitivity table and identify the break-even commit size. Also call out the incremental cost to support 128k: likely small fixed cost for a tiny pool but higher per-token compute  show absolute $/1M for those requests separately.

I’ll help pull kernel/throughput numbers for the model family they plan to use (ask Marissa which model variant).

-Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
